newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, spreads to U.S. narrow.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, spreads to U.S. narrow.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Monday with a softer U.S. bond market weighing on prices, even as spreads to U.S. bonds tumbled to their lowest levels in years, analysts said.

"Most of the international markets are de-coupling from the U.S.," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities. "We can because most people think that we're going to be announcing a current account surplus this week." Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 rose C$0.13 to C$102.45 to yield 7.779 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 15/32 to yield 6.99 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 79 basis points and from 82 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

The spread between the Canadian and U.S. 30-year benchmarkets is now at its lowest point in more than two years and spread narrowing is taking place along the yield curve, analysts said. Canadian five-year bond yields today traded below U.S. yields for the first time since the 1980's.

Analysts said many investors were looking ahead to the release on Friday of the current account for the second quarter. Many expect the report to show a current account surplus for the first time in more than a decade.
A current account surplus could strengthen the currency and provide support for the Canadian bond market, analysts said.

In new issues, Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corporation, a federally guaranteed issuing agency, issued a C$65 million 6.25 percent bond due September 4, 2001 at a retail price of C$99.249, lead manager RBC Dominion Securities Inc said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.04 to C$97.65 to yield 7.328 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 10/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 53 basis points from 58 basis points near the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 4.02 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.18 percent.
